- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive or neutral (especially after recent spikes), especially in early forecast periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or volatile (especially after sharp drops), particularly in mid-to-late forecast windows.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if history shows recent price consolidation, forecast should not overshoot beyond 1–2% of recent range.
- Reduce forecast magnitude after sentiment turns negative (e.g., sentiment < 0.3) — model tends to overreact.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts when sentiment is mixed or trending sideways — model often assumes continuation.
- Adjust downward if forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by a 3–5 day decline in sentiment — model tends to overcorrect.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is below 0.5 over last 5 days — indicates weakening momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently above 0.7, model tends to overpredict — apply a 1–2% downward bias to avoid “sentiment inflation.”
